slots.title: Oil slips after hours-long U.S.–Iran UN meeting
slots.body:
$USO closed down 2.8% at 144.08.

Brent crude futures finished at 98.80, down 0.5% on the day.

CNBC tied the move to Tuesday’s U.S.–Iran talks at the UN, where Trump said he faces a big decision on a deal with Tehran versus further escalation.

What would you watch first if those talks stay on the calendar?

slots.title: Fed still fighting inflation above 2% target
slots.body:
The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.0% in the latest FMP snapshot dated 2026-09-18.

The gap between 2-year (4.8%) and 10-year (5.0%) yields was 0.25 percentage points on that same date — a relatively flat shape between those two points on the curve.

Fox Business framed the backdrop as inflation still above the Fed’s 2% goal, with the central bank having raised rates and traders weighing additional increases through year-end.

How do you read “not declaring victory” against where the 10-year yield is sitting?

slots.title: Financials under pressure, yield curve in focus
slots.body:
Reuters said the S&P 500 Financial index and the benchmark’s bank group were under pressure in Tuesday’s session.

The story linked that weakness to worries about artificial intelligence competing with traditional finance, uncertainty around AI-related IPOs, and moves in the bond market.

On the FMP treasury snapshot from 2026-09-18, the 2-year yield was 4.8% and the 10-year was 5.0%, for a 2s10s spread of 0.25.

Which part of that mix — AI, IPOs, or rates — do you think showed up most in the price action you saw?

slots.title: Banks slide 3% on AI, bond-spread worries
slots.body:

- $V -2.1% to 362.04

Which part of the financials complex stood out most to you today — banks or card networks?

slots.title: US close — Sept. 22, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led the major U.S. indexes, closing up 0.5% at 27,244.28 with a session high of 27,288.79 matching the 52-week high in the data.
That made a second consecutive record close a central story in the day’s market coverage.

The S&P 500 ended essentially flat at 7,764.27 (0.0% on a rounded basis).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4% to 51,863.69.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% to 2,889.92, so smaller caps tracked the Nasdaq more than the Dow.

Financial stocks were among the heaviest weights on the benchmark narrative.
Bank of America ($BAC) closed down 3.0% at 56.20, and Mastercard ($MA) and Visa ($V) each lost 2.1%, to 555.89 and 362.04.
The Nasdaq financial services sector averaged about -1.7%, aligning with reports that cited AI-related competition worries and bond-market structure.

Technology was the strongest sector in the injected sector table, up about 1.8% on average.
NVIDIA ($NVDA) gained 0.7% to 228.87, Taiwan Semiconductor ($TSM) rose 1.5% to 452.00, and Intel ($INTC) added 1.7% to 123.86.
Microsoft ($MSFT) and Alphabet ($GOOGL) were modest decliners, at -0.7% (498.00) and -1.1% (351.16).

Consumer and healthcare names showed selective strength.
Walmart ($WMT) rose 2.5% to 110.12.
Eli Lilly ($LLY) gained 0.5% to 1,170.48.
PepsiCo ($PEP) was up 1.2% to 131.19.
Tesla ($TSLA) closed up 1.0% at 378.90.

AutoZone ($AZO) reported results on the calendar: EPS of about 0.56 versus an estimate near 0.54, on revenue of about $6.59 billion versus an estimate near $6.70 billion.
The share price finished up 3.3% at 2,894.73.

Energy and shipping names reflected softer crude.
$USO fell 2.8% to 144.08 and Brent was down 0.5% to 98.75 after U.S.–Iran meeting headlines.
EuroDry ($EDRY) fell 20.4% to 54.08, and the Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF ($BWET) lost 18.2% to 682.01.

On the economic calendar, Richmond Fed manufacturing index printed -2 versus a +5 estimate, and manufacturing shipments were -5 versus +9 expected.
Services index was 0 versus -6 expected.
Redbook year-over-year sales growth was 7.6% versus 8.5% prior.
API crude oil stocks rose 1.786 million barrels versus a -0.5 million estimate.
The 2-year note auction cleared at 4.8%.
August M2 money supply was reported at 23.34 trillion.
Several Fed speakers were scheduled (Williams, Jefferson, Barkin).

Cross-asset, the VIX fell 4.4% to 14.21.
Gold futures were down 0.1% at 4,372.40.
The dollar proxy ($UUP) was unchanged at 28.48.
Bitcoin rose 0.4% to 86,576.60.
The latest Treasury snapshot in the data (dated 2026-09-18) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.25.

Overseas, the Nikkei 225 rose 1.4% to 65,018.95.
The Hang Seng fell 0.9% to 24,860.50.
The FTSE 100 slipped 0.3% to 10,708.33.
